name: Coldwall Combat Boot (Shelf Cut)
description: A mid-calf boot built from scrap leather panels stitched together with visible, uneven seams — some waxed thread, some monofilament pulled from cable housings. The lacing is mismatched: two different eyelet systems, one side using a knotted cord in place of a missing hook. The soles are thick and aggressive, cut from truck tire tread and bonded with contact cement.
functionality: Exceptional grip on wet metal and concrete. Ankle support is moderate.
what_it_says: You made these yourself, or you know someone who did. The Shelf takes care of its own.
worn_by: anyone who can't get to a market
story_hooks: The leather panels came from at least three different sources — one strip is stamped with a corporate access badge logo.
Someone in the Shelf is known for their distinctive stitching pattern. These boots can be traced back to them.
